content_type: Video tutorial transcript (Claude AI + Claude Code + Claude Co-Work)
doctrine: Comprehensive operating manual for Claude across three interfaces (Chat, Code, Co-Work). Two video segments distilled: segs 1-10 cover prompt architecture and workspace setup; segs 11-16 cover autonomous agent workflows, token management, and deployment. Junk-to-gold ratio: ~30-40% boilerplate across full doc. All actionable mechanics extracted below.
operating_rules: 90% of users use AI wrong: specificity beats generality. Generic = garbage output; specific = leverage.
Three-part prompt structure required: Instructions (what to do) + Context (full background, data, examples) + Constraints (rules, style, tone, format, length). Always use this shape.
Mega-prompt generation: ask Claude to write the detailed prompt for you, then feed that prompt back. Let AI do the prompt-engineering work.
Ground-First-Ask-Second: separate the research task from the synthesis task. Search first, let knowledge inform, then synthesize. Never combine in one step when currency of data matters.
Add to every non-trivial prompt: 'Are there any missing context or details I should provide to improve this answer?' Catches gaps before output.
Context window is your operational ceiling. Token budget governs everything; stay aware.
System tools overhead: ~16,800 tokens consumed by Claude Code default tools before user sends first message. Always billed; unavoidable.
System prompt (CLAUDE.md global + local): ~10,000 tokens baseline per session.
MEMORY.md auto-loaded every session: minimize to 2-5k tokens max. Bloated memory is wasted budget.
Message overhead = only ~2.6-3% of total context. Majority consumed by system infrastructure (tools, MCP, memory). Optimize inputs for information density, not message count.
Auto-compact triggers at ~33k tokens remaining (~99% context full). Manual /compact available anytime.
MCP tools add context overhead (5-20% depending on server complexity). Use sparingly. If MCP exceeds 10% of context window, switch to tool-search load-on-demand mode.
Agent teams cost 7x more tokens than standard sessions. Parallelization trades cost for speed. Know when the tradeoff is worth it.
Git worktrees eliminate cross-agent file conflicts. Each agent works isolated branch, merges to main. Git's conflict management becomes the coordination layer.
Skills load on-demand; don't consume context until invoked. Projects bake context in permanently (skills + CLAUDE.md + memory). One project per recurring workflow.
Scheduled tasks run on host machine when desktop app is open. No external APIs or third-party automation needed. Test manually first, then schedule.
Sub-agent cost optimization: use Sonnet for heavy lifting sub-agents (cheaper, longer context), Opus for orchestration. Never burn Opus tokens on repetitive/low-intelligence tasks.
Web search must always be enabled for research-oriented tasks. Default on.
Desktop app preferred over browser: faster, better plugin/skill support.
Project memory compounds: first session = generic, second = refined, Nth = highly customized. Projects are state machines; each iteration improves baseline.
Custom instructions persist across all conversations in a project. Set once; never re-explain.
named_methods: Three-Part Prompt Formula (Instructions + Context + Constraints): the universal prompt shape. Never send a prompt without all three.
Mega-Prompt Generation: let Claude write a detailed prompt for the task, then use that prompt as the actual query. Compound specificity without manual effort.
Ground-First-Ask-Second: research task first (web search, file read), synthesis second. Separates information-gathering from reasoning.
Plan Mode: plan before executing. Front-load research; eliminate wasted loops during build. Reduces token waste significantly.

Context Compaction: progressive summarization of conversation history at ~99% full. 'Netlify Rebuilds' becomes 'Netlify Rebuilding' = same info, fewer tokens. Compression increases information density, not just shrinks size.
Agent Teams Framework: spawn N parallel agents on separate tasks/branches, then merge. Include adversarial debate agents (devil's advocate) for review quality. Borrowed from GAN precedent.
Adversarial Debate Pattern: spawn 2 debate agents (devil 1: 'findings not real', devil 2: 'findings real + need fixing'), have them argue to consensus. Higher quality than single-agent review.
Git Worktrees: multiple isolated working directories sharing Git history. Each agent/branch works independently, merges to main. Eliminates cross-agent stepping.
Proposal Generator Pattern: voice transcript + prompt + Claude Code = landing page + proposal object deployed to Netlify. 15-20 min end-to-end. Replaces Panda Doc at near-zero cost.
Skills-to-URL Pipeline: skill definition (Markdown checklist) + Modal API wrapper = public webhook. 2-minute setup. Form-based skill invocation.
Co-Work Projects Pattern: persistent folder + context MD files (about-me, brand-voice, working-preferences) auto-loaded every session. Memory compounds; no re-explaining.
Scheduled Task Automation: write prompt once, set cadence (daily/weekly/monthly), Claude executes on schedule. Dispatch (SMS/mobile) allows remote task submission to desktop runner.
Token Optimization via Sub-Agents: Sonnet for sub-agents doing heavy/repetitive work, Opus for orchestration. Saves tokens where throughput > intelligence.

Skills vs. Scripts distinction: skill = Markdown instruction file with optional code (loads on-demand), script = inline code (always present). Use skills for reusable workflows; scripts for task-specific logic.
specific_numbers: Sonnet / newer models context window: 1-2,000,000 tokens
System tools overhead: ~16,800 tokens (always consumed, unavoidable)
Agent teams token multiplier: 7x vs. standard session
Security audit agent team example: 10 scanner agents + 4 documentation agents + 2 debate agents + 15 fixer agents = 1.3M tokens, ~$80, saved weeks of developer time
Lead scrape skill: 1,000 leads in 87 seconds (parallel). Previous manual time: 30-60 minutes
Invoice summarizer: 5 invoices processed in 4 minutes. Manual time: 2-3 hours
Modal API credits on signup: $5-30 free. Ongoing: $0.30 per 1M tokens
Netlify deployment cost: free tier (no cost beyond Claude Code tokens)
Opus 4.6 fast mode: 2.5x faster execution, 3x cost
Website builder agent team: 7-8 design variants, 150k-200k tokens
YouTube content project setup time: ~4-5 minutes (folder + skills + projects + scheduled tasks)

Invoice Summarizer: reads PDF invoices, categorizes into folders, creates Excel with totals/taxes/subtotals. Time: 4 min / 5 invoices. Manual equiv: 2-3 hours.
Client Meeting Processor: transcripts -> extract action items -> spreadsheet with auto-calculated deadlines + draft follow-up emails. Output: ready-to-send email + tracking sheet.
Content Research Briefing: daily 9 AM, search trending AI automation topics (past 7 days), identify 3 video concepts, save brief, post summary to Slack.
Morning Briefing: daily 6 AM, check Gmail (past 12 hr unread), check Google Calendar (today), summarize to morning-brief.md. 2 hours of pre-work automated before waking.
Apollo Prospecting: find leads via Apollo.io connector, enrich data, load into sequences.
YouTube Script Writer: scripts matching user tone, hooks, structure, channel performance patterns. Loaded via project context.
Website Builder (Agent Teams): design 3-4 variants in parallel, user picks, spin up 4 more iterations. 7-8 designs total. Token cost: 150k-200k.
OpenClaw Security Auditor: 10 scanner agents + 4 documentation agents + 2 debate agents + 15 fixer agents. Parallel codebase review. 1.3M tokens, 15-20 min research, saved weeks of manual time.
prompts: Mega-prompt template: 'Can you create a detailed prompt in order to [task]? Generate me a prompt that will research [domain], find best opportunities and methods that can [outcome]. Do deep research and create a prompt.'
Three-part structure template: [INSTRUCTIONS: define what to do] + [CONTEXT: full background/data/examples] + [CONSTRAINTS: rules/style/tone/format/length]
Context-eliciting close: 'Are there any missing context or details I should provide to improve this answer?'
Ground-first pattern: 'Research [topic] and make sure you are up to date on all capabilities, then [synthesis task].'
Custom instruction example: 'Do not put bullet points in any output. Always include warm closing. Frame answers for web design industry.'
Token density instruction (add to CLAUDE.md): 'Write as succinctly as possible. Reason privately. When outputting, give bare-bones info. If I need more, I will ask.'
Proposal generator seed: [voice transcript] + 'Claude, make me a landing page + proposal object. I send 4-5/day. Turn this into a one-shot voice transcript -> AI prompt -> generated landing page.'

Agent teams security audit: 'This repo has security issues. I don't know where. Create a team of 10 to search the codebase. Split logically by file size. Add 4 documentation agents + 2 debate agents (devil's advocate). Use Sonnet for longer context. When done, 1 agent per issue to fix. No overlapping work; if agents step on toes, have them rectify via conversation.'
Git worktrees setup: 'I have [repo]. I want to design 3 new pages in parallel. Use Git worktrees so each agent works on a separate branch, then merge. Provide clear instructions in CLAUDE.md.'
Skills to URL (Modal): 'Deploy the [skill] as a public URL. User fills form, skill runs, CSV downloads. Remove auth. Use Modal.'

Co-Work setup: 'Give me a folder structure (context, projects, output). Create about-me.md, brand-voice.md, working-preferences.md. Ask me questions to populate. Store in context folder. Auto-load every session.'
Morning briefing schedule: '/schedule | daily 6 AM | check Gmail (12 hr unread), check Google Calendar (today), summarize to morning-brief.md | save to daily-briefings folder'
Content research schedule: '/schedule | daily 9 AM | search trending [topic] (past 7 days), identify 3 video opportunities, save research-brief.md to project, post summary to Slack'
Website builder iterative: 'Design 3 website variants for [brief]. I will pick one. Spin up 4 more iterations on the one I like. Keep going until I pick the final one.'
Status line setup: '/status-line | include loading bar with token usage (X% of 200k)'
gates: Security gate (before any public deployment): developer security review pass required. Cost: few hundred dollars. Without it: exposed passwords, payment data, emails.
Token spend gate (before agent teams): estimate spend, ensure budget absorbs it. $80 for 15-min audit saving weeks of dev time = good ROI. $1.3M tokens for uncertain benefit = wasteful.
Skill evaluation gate (before production): manually test output quality. Skills don't guarantee accuracy; human review confirms before automation runs.
Context monitoring gate (recurring): run /context every 2-3 sessions. If MCP overhead exceeds 10% of context, reduce server count.
Project setup gate: only create projects for tasks done 2+ times. Single-use tasks = chat or co-work session, not project.
Scheduled task test gate: run prompt manually, review output, tweak until perfect. Then schedule. Prevents broken automations from looping.
Merge conflict gate (agent team merges): orchestration agent reviews all merge diffs before committing to main. Prevents silent data corruption.
weird_gold: Adversarial debate agents borrow from GAN (generative adversarial network) ML precedent. Two agents argue findings to consensus. Higher quality than single-agent review. Directly applicable to any quality-critical workflow.
Context compaction increases information density, not just shrinks size. 'Netlify Rebuilds' -> 'Netlify Rebuilding' = same info, fewer tokens. Counter-intuitive: compression improves output quality.
Dispatch (SMS remote control): text Claude from phone, task runs on desktop, push notification when done. Phone is UI; desktop is compute. Inverts typical mobile app paradigm.
Project memory as state machine: each session improves baseline. By Nth session, output is highly customized. Compounding returns on context investment.
Worktree isolation pattern: Git's conflict management becomes agent coordination layer. No explicit inter-agent communication needed for parallel file work.
Sub-agent intelligence tiering: Sonnet for throughput (categorization, data entry, code fixes), Opus for orchestration (planning, judgment). Explicit cost-intelligence tradeoff.
Skills as instruction files vs. scripts as inline code: skills load on-demand (zero context cost until invoked), scripts always present (always token cost). Heavy-lifting logic in skills = efficient.
Trivial API endpoints (birthday check) teach the core pattern that scales to complex business logic (webhooks, data processing, payment flows). Start trivial, apply everywhere.
Scrape leads skill: 1,000 leads in 87 seconds via parallel processing. Manual equivalent: 30-60 minutes. This is the 'show don't tell' ROI proof for agent parallelization.
contradictions: Token cost philosophy: early framing says 'cost is unavoidable, plan spend' (agent teams $80 example); later optimization section emphasizes minimize spend via compression. No clear decision rule for when to spend vs. optimize.
Agent autonomy risk: agent teams shown as powerful but also 'nuclear weapon aimed at your wallet.' Mitigation strategies (cost caps, per-agent token limits) not detailed.
Skills reusability ceiling: skills presented as high-ROI but video shows manual steps post-execution (form filling, result review). Skill doesn't fully automate; human still in loop for quality.
Context management priority: /compact presented as must-do early, then as optional advanced technique later. Prioritization inconsistent.
Desktop vs. browser ambiguity: desktop recommended for skills but browser also shown as option. No hard rule on when browser is sufficient.
Extended thinking position: sometimes framed as fallback, sometimes as default for complex tasks. No clear decision threshold.
notes: Full doc = 16 segments. Segs 1-10 = Claude Chat/UI fundamentals. Segs 11-16 = Claude Code + Co-Work advanced operations. High signal across both halves. Specific numbers and named methods are the most extractable value. Adversarial debate pattern and compaction-as-density-increase are the two non-obvious insights. All prompts above are copy-paste ready.
